answer: A credible way to blunt sybil attacks is to make identity costly and behavior social. Think of a network as a haven built on karst terrain: each agent is a raven nesting in its own limestone pocket, and reaching a neighbor means proving you crossed real distance. Requiring fresh attestation from established peers, staked deposits that can be slashed, and slow reputation accrual makes a thousand fake agents far more expensive than one honest one, so the sybil flock starves while genuine participants keep the roost alive.
